units.translation: Absyrtus from her bed, Jason having told her, and to bring him to the Argonauts; and when they were pursued, to slaughter him and, having cut him limb from limb, to cast him into the river. But in the Scythians Sophocles says that Absyrtus was not of the same mother as Medea (fr. 546 Pearson): 'For they did not spring from one bed, but he was the child of a Nereid, just born, while her Eidyia, daughter of Oceanus, had borne before.'

b. The ship now with mighty: The ship, he says, was accomplishing its voyage with violent impulse, driven both by the strength of the rowers and by the current of the river drawing it down.
d. But the king in his folly: Aeetes, he says, having fallen into many misfortunes, called upon Helios and Zeus as witnesses of what had been done.

Apollonius says through these lines that Aeetes returned without success, and through the following lines (v. 224 ff.) he says that Absyrtus, being young, rode as charioteer beside his father. But Dionysius of Miletus (32 fr. 10a J.) says that Aeetes pursued them; the chiefs fought by hurling javelins, while those around Aeetes rode on horseback; there Iphis, son of Sthenelus, also died; for after striking down two of the horsemen around Aeetes, he was surrounded by Aeetes and dragged off with a noose. In the following lines he says that the Colchians turned to flight. Pherecydes in Book 7 (3 fr. 32b J.) says that when they were pursued, they brought Absyrtus onto the ship, cut him limb from limb, and threw him into the river. Sophocles in the Colchian Women (fr. 343 Pearson) says that the boy was slaughtered in the house of Aeetes. Next Apollonius places the threat against the Colchians.

247-52. And indeed all that with sacrifice: From this he wishes to make clear that she intended to perform such a sacrifice as sorceresses do. Nymphis in the sixth book of his work On Heraclea (fr. 14 M. III 15) says that there is a sanctuary of Hecate in Paphlagonia founded by Medea. By the aposiopesis he employs emphasis, not elaborating on the sacrifice performed by sorceresses.
